Article Title: Bangladesh wage protests: Clashes erupt between garment workers and police, dozens of factories shut
Article Text:

Tensions escalated in Bangladesh's Ashulia on Saturday as garment workers demanding a hike in minimum wages clashed with security forces. Police fired tear gas to disperse the protesters and bring the situation under control, The Daily Star reported.According to the news agency ANI, the confrontation took place around 11 am in the Kathgara area along the Zirabo-Bismail road. Workers from several garment factories had stopped production and joined the protest, according to the report.Eyewitnesses told The daily star that workers at multiple factories in Kathgara first entered their workplaces before stopping work. They later organised a rally and attempted to block the road around 10:45 am after factory management announced holidays.Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police at industrial police-1 in Ashulia, said in a text message around noon that the situation had returned to normal."Some unruly workers were trying to create instability at the garment factories that remained operational in the Kathgara area. Industrial police and other forces intervened to keep the situation under control," Bhuiyan said.Earlier on Saturday, at least 50 factories in the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt announced holidays following work stoppages.However, most factories in the area had started operations as usual in the morning, industrial police told the newspaper.The latest clashes come amid continuing protests by garment workers across Bangladesh over demands for higher wages and better working conditions.On Tuesday, garment workers staged demonstrations in Mirpur, Dhaka, demanding that the minimum monthly wage be increased to 30,000 taka. The protests came as labour unrest spread across the country's textile industry, forcing several factories to suspend operations.Protesters also attempted to block roads but were stopped by police, who intervened to prevent traffic disruptions and maintain law and order.Garment workers in several parts of Bangladesh have been staging strikes to demand better pay, with demonstrations leading to factory closures in multiple industrial areas, DW reported.Separately, a group of workers gathered at Padmar Mor in the Hemayetpur area of Savar around 3 pm on Monday, briefly disrupting the area. Police asked them to disperse peacefully, following which they cleared the road without further incident, Dhaka Tribune reported.Meanwhile, around 40 factories remained closed in the Savar and Ashulia industrial zones on Monday, according to industrial police.Of these, 27 factories were shut under section 13(1) of the Bangladesh labour act, while nine were declared closed indefinitely. The remaining factories observed general holidays.Bhuiyan said workers at one factory refused to resume work after the lunch break and continued sitting inside the premises, prompting management to declare a holiday. Employees at two other factories also stopped work and staged sit-in protests inside their workplaces.However, workers at other factories across the industrial areas continued their operations peacefully, he added.
Article Summary: Police fired tear gas to disperse the protesters and bring the situation under control. The confrontation took place around 11 am in the Kathgara area along the Zirabo-Bismail road. Workers from several garment factories had stopped production and joined the protest.

Article Title: A Pennsylvania mother died in 2019 and left her home to her son, who died in 2023; the county then sold it for $109,000 after sending tax-sale notices to the dead mother, but a court ordered the sale
Article Text:
Representative Image (AI-generated)

Mother left the property to her son in her will

County sold the home for $109,000

Court finds county failed to investigate

Appeals court orders tax sale to be set aside

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A Pennsylvania appeals court has ordered the cancellation of a $109,000 tax sale of a family home after finding that county officials failed to investigate notices returned with the word "Deceased". The property in Garnet Valley had belonged to Bonnie Wilson, who died in December 2019 and left the home to her son, Kevin Wilson, through her will. Kevin also died in August 2023, just weeks before the county's September tax sale. However, the Delaware County Tax Claim Bureau continued sending notices addressed to his deceased mother and did not make reasonable efforts to establish who owned the property. In a November 19, 2026 decision , available on Justia, the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court reversed a lower court's ruling and directed that the sale be set aside.Bonnie Wilson purchased the property at 5103 Poplar Street in Garnet Valley, Delaware County, in June 2017. She lived there until her death in December 2019, when the home passed to her son, Kevin, under her will. Kevin also lived at the property. The property subsequently became subject to delinquent real estate taxes for 2021 and 2022. According to the court record, the county's Tax Claim Bureau continued to treat Bonnie as the property's owner because its records at the Recorder of Deeds and Board of Assessment still listed her name.In 2022, the bureau sent a certified-mail notice about the unpaid taxes to Bonnie at the property address. The letter was returned as unclaimed and unable to be forwarded. The bureau sent another notice in July 2023, informing her of the upcoming tax sale. This time, the letter was sent by certified mail with restricted delivery. A postal receipt was returned with an illegible signature. Meanwhile, Kevin had died on or about August 7, 2023. His will was probated on August 24, and Kelli A Barth was appointed executrix of his estate.Despite the earlier returned correspondence, the bureau proceeded with the tax sale scheduled for September 21, 2023. In August, it sent a final notice to Bonnie by first-class mail. That letter was returned on August 29 with a handwritten notation stating "Deceased". This was almost a month before the scheduled sale.A deputy sheriff also reportedly posted the property and personally served Kevin with notice on July 24, 2023. However, Kevin had already died by the time the sale took place. The bureau nevertheless proceeded with the auction, and CJD Group LLC emerged as the successful bidder, purchasing the property for $109,000.After the sale, another notice addressed to Bonnie was returned with the postal notation "Deceased". During testimony, the bureau's upset tax sale coordinator, Janine Heinlein, acknowledged that this was the first time the office had any indication that Bonnie was no longer alive. She also admitted that the final notice sent before the sale had already been returned with the same notation. Barth learned that the property had been sold only on October 5, 2023, when she signed an agreement to sell it and her realtor informed her of the tax auction.Barth challenged the sale, arguing that the bureau had failed to follow Pennsylvania's Real Estate Tax Sale Law. However, the Delaware County Court of Common Pleas rejected her petition, finding that the bureau had met its notification obligations. The dispute then reached the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court.The appeals court focused on Section 607.1 of the Real Estate Tax Sale Law, which requires tax claim bureaus to make reasonable efforts to locate property owners when notices are returned without personal signatures or other circumstances raise significant doubts about whether the intended recipient received them. The court found that the repeated notices returned with the word "Deceased" should have prompted further investigation. The bureau could have contacted the Register of Wills to establish whether Bonnie's estate had been probated, whether ownership had changed and who was entitled to receive notice.Instead, it proceeded with the sale without making those enquiries. The court also rejected CJD Group's argument that the sheriff's personal service on Kevin was sufficient. Kevin had died more than a month before the auction, making that notification ineffective.In its November 19, 2026 ruling, the Commonwealth Court reversed the lower court's decision and remanded the case with instructions to enter an order setting aside the tax sale. The judges emphasised that the responsibility for complying with statutory notification requirements rests with the tax claim bureau, rather than being determined by whether the property owner or estate representatives had been diligent.The ruling does not mean that unpaid property taxes can be disregarded. Instead, it establishes that a tax sale cannot stand when the responsible government agency fails to make the additional notification efforts required by law after receiving clear indications that its notices are not reaching the property owner. For the Wilson family, the decision means the $109,000 auction sale must be set aside, returning the dispute to the lower court for the required order.
Article Summary: Pennsylvania appeals court orders cancellation of $109,000 tax sale of family home. Court finds county officials failed to investigate notices returned with the word "Deceased" The property in Garnet Valley had belonged to Bonnie Wilson, who died in December 2019. She left the home to her son, Kevin Wilson, through her will. Kevin also died in August 2023, just weeks before the county's September tax sale.

Article Title: Ex-Trump press secretary Katie Zacharia under probe for posing as lawyer without passing bar
Article Text:
Ex-White House press secretary Katie Zacharia.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is facing an investigation by the State Bar of California over allegations that she presented herself as a qualified lawyer despite never passing a bar examination in the United States.The investigation follows a complaint filed in October by Campaign for Accountability, a non-profit watchdog organisation. The California bar informed the group earlier this month that an investigator and legal adviser had been assigned to examine the allegations.Before joining the Trump administration, Zacharia appeared on several television programmes and described herself as a lawyer. Her LinkedIn profile also listed her as the general counsel of a California-based non-profit organisation. Trump referred to her as an “attorney” when announcing her appointment as White House press secretary.Although Zacharia graduated from Pepperdine University with a law degree in 2011, she has not passed the bar examination in California or any other US state, according to The Guardian.Michelle Kuppersmith, director of Campaign for Accountability, questioned Zacharia's repeated claims about her professional credentials.“Zacharia may have thought she was just playing a lawyer on TV, but by repeatedly holding herself out as an attorney on news programs, she was pretending to have authority she lacks,” Kuppersmith said.“We’re pleased the California bar is taking this matter seriously and investigating,” she added.Zacharia has rejected the allegations. A spokesperson for her told The Guardian: “These are baseless allegations. This complaint is politically motivated and a clear waste of the state bar’s time and resources. We are confident it will be dismissed with no finding of wrongdoing.”Zacharia had earlier defended her use of the term “lawyer”, arguing that it was distinct from “attorney”, which she said referred to someone licensed to practise law. In an email to the newspaper, she cited an American Bar Association Journal article discussing the distinction between the two terms.A spokesperson for the State Bar of California confirmed that it was aware of reports concerning Zacharia, describing her as a non-licensee. However, the spokesperson stressed that an investigation or complaint does not establish that someone has engaged in the unauthorised practice of law or violated state statutes. The bar also said its investigations remain confidential.Campaign for Accountability had urged the regulator to examine whether Zacharia misrepresented her qualifications to the public and determine whether she violated California law.The controversy follows Zacharia's brief tenure as Trump's press secretary. She replaced Karoline Leavitt in mid-October but left the position after five days, making her the shortest-serving person to hold the role. During her first press briefing, she stumbled over some of her remarks and took questions primarily from conservative media outlets.
Article Summary: Former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is facing an investigation by the State Bar of California. The investigation follows a complaint filed in October by Campaign for Accountability. Zacharia graduated from Pepperdine University with a law degree in 2011. She has not passed the bar examination in California or any other US state.

Article Title: 7 killed as tribal feud over forest ownership triggers gunfight in Pakistan
Article Text:
4 from one tribe, 3 from another killed in Pakistan forest ownership clash

Seven people were killed in a clash between two tribes over the ownership of a forest in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, news agency PTI reported, quoting police Saturday.The incident took place around 10pm local time on Thursday at Bilija forest in Battagram district, when armed members of the Gilal and Kaloch tribes confronted each other, leading to an exchange of gunfire.According to police, armed men from the Kaloch tribe took positions and opened fire, prompting retaliation from the Gilal side. Four members of the Gilal tribe and three from the Kaloch tribe were killed in the clash.The two tribes have been involved in a longstanding dispute over the ownership of Bilija forest, which has continued for several decades and claimed several lives in the past, police said.The Gilal tribe is associated with the Allai valley in Battagram district, while the Kaloch community belongs to neighbouring Kohistan district.Police said repeated efforts by the administrations of both districts to resolve the dispute and bring the communities together had failed to produce a permanent solution.The latest clash has once again raised concerns over the law and order situation in Imran Khan 's stronghold Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Article Summary: Four members of the Gilal tribe and three from the Kaloch tribe were killed in the clash. The two tribes have been involved in a longstanding dispute over the ownership of Bilija forest. The latest clash has once again raised concerns over the law and order situation in Imran Khan's stronghold Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Article Title: More than 100,000 strangers have shared handwritten stories anonymously; what do their confessions reveal about loneliness, grief, love and hope?
Article Text:
A representative image of The Strangers Project's exhibition (credit: Canva AI )

A collage of a select few notes shared with the project. (Image credit: Substack/ The Strangers Project)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

“My family needs this exhibit,” said a stranger. “Life has felt like a beautiful thriller,” said another. Some parts of our lives, the most dangerous and guarded corners of our worlds, are often the easiest to reach into when we know we may be heard, seen or, in the case of The Strangers Project , read.Stories have travelled far and wide since the beginning of time. Words have been caught between strange worlds, woven by strangers, making their way into myths, orature and, most often, simply explaining the absurdities of life itself. But why, in a world of notes apps, comments and chat boxes, do we yearn to disperse ourselves in ink on paper? Why must we write, and why must we remember?Brandon Doman first started the project in 2009 with a simple idea: to collect stories, something palpable and tangible, shared by hand on a page, always in person and always anonymously. Today, with the project having gathered over 100,000 stories, the world is met with a living repository. It is an art installation of what it is simply to be human, and of the condition we are all ridden with: life. You can now find Doman collecting stories from Thursday to Sunday, between 2 and 6:30 pm, at the project's semi-installation at the World Trade Center Oculus in New York City, USA.“Exploring the lives of the people we share space with every day shows us how wonderfully human we all are.These stories engage strangers of all ages and backgrounds to reflect, rejoice, heal and connect through words,” Doman writes on the project's website.“You cannot practice love with someone you don’t love,” writes someone who has visited The Strangers Project wall for the fifth time. As life has changed, so has their perspective on love, and the words seem almost like a reminder to slowly bandage a hurting, broken heart that is beginning to heal. Some confessions are written to speak to parts of who we once were when we were in love, as we struggle with the little griefs that accompany it. Because while remembering may hurt too much, being reminded can feel almost necessary, like a repair, a fix.“I have a dream to be a singer and I will not let haters bring me down!” writes a girl from Toronto. Written with equal parts courage and kindness, the confession carries the yearning of a heart holding on to a dream. Some dreams necessitate a fire within us, a determination to keep going, and an insatiable hunger even when the world may not always be kind. And so, anonymously as it may be, this is a little declaration of hope, written down for the world to read.“I forgive you. I know you raised me the best you could. As a Black man, I know being vulnerable was hard for you,” writes a son to his father. Growing up in a world that demands so much of you, especially because of how you identify, can shape the relationships you carry with you. In these words, a son seems to wrestle with the challenges of the father he had and the son he now chooses to be.“I lost my Best Friend…TELL THEM ‘I LOVE YOU’. SAY I LOVE YOU before it is too late.” Across these pages, you find smatterings of feelings left unsaid. While one person writes to forgive, another is still remembering, holding on to words that perhaps never found their way to the person they were meant for. So writes a grieving person, with love that is immense and grief that clings and refuses to leave. While this pain tends to follow us, its imprint may take the shape of love. When your heart aches for what you have lost, perhaps you can still find your way back to the love you have, especially on the days you forget to put it into words.“I feel some freedom knowing we are all in this together, and knowing how minor most things are in the scope of history, our life’s journey, let alone the history of humankind!” There is a certain freedom in knowing that, despite the different lives we lead and the different things we carry, we are all part of something much larger. Our worries, our griefs, our little triumphs and our dreams may feel like the entirety of our worlds when we are living through them, but somewhere, in another corner of the world, someone else is feeling, remembering and hoping too.In big, black, bold letters, the words “This space is for you” spread across the project’s site, where you are instantly acknowledged and spoken to. While some of us yearn to be seen, others wish to shrink, hide or slowly dissipate. The project’s space, by design, rushes to embrace you, gently nudging you to sit with whatever you may be feeling.Despite the different people we may be, our life stories can tether us to the people we may never meet, see or hear, but whose lives will compel us to look at our own. We are all just carriers of our own weight, but when, on bad days, you seem to forget the immense joy, gratitude and hope you carry; take it one day at a time, and if forlornness catches you, take it one story at a time.Perhaps this is what the stranger meant when they wrote, “My family needs this exhibit.” There is something to be revelled in about a space that asks so little of you, yet allows you to leave so much behind. A place where defences can fall away, where you can sit almost armourless with yourself.If you had to reach into the quiet corners of your life and write it down, what might it be? And which part of you will you write to today?
Article Summary: Brandon Doman started The Strangers Project in 2009 with a simple idea: to collect stories, something palpable and tangible, shared by hand on a page. Today, with the project having gathered over 100,000 stories, the world is met with a living repository. You can now find Doman collecting stories from Thursday to Sunday, between 2 and 6:30 pm, at the project's semi-installation at the World Trade Center Oculus.

A massive fire ripped through a commercial building on Thailand's southern resort island of Phuket early on Monday, killing at least 11 people and leaving 16 others injured, police told Reuters. The blaze broke out in the early hours of the morning and quickly spread to several nearby buildings, triggering a major firefighting operation.The fire erupted at around 3.17am local time (2017 GMT) at a shophouse housing a vehicle rental business. Firefighters battled the flames for nearly two hours before bringing the blaze under control, Thai authorities said.Of the 16 injured, 15 were Thai nationals while one was from Myanmar, police said. No tourists were among those killed or injured in the incident.The building is located in a town area near Patong, one of Phuket's most popular beach destinations on the island's western coast. The incident raised concerns as the fire spread beyond the building where it first broke out, engulfing several neighbouring structures.The cause of the fire remains under investigation, with authorities yet to establish what triggered the blaze.The incident comes just four months after a deadly fire at a bar in Bangkok claimed at least 27 lives, highlighting another major fire tragedy in Thailand.Make the intro more directRemove repeated fire detailsUse a sharper news structure

Article Title: GTA 6 release: Nearly 1 in 5 US workers plan to take time off to play
Article Text:
GTA 6 release: Nearly 1 in 5 US workers plan to take time off to play

Lander Allgood and Connor Folkers plan extended breaks for GTA 6 release

GTA flu: Why some gamers are planning to call in sick

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nearly one in five salaried workers in the United States plans to take time off for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday, November 19. Some have already booked their paid leave, while others are considering calling in sick to spend the day playing the long-awaited game. A GameSquare survey also found that 36% of workers considering time off would rather call in sick than request leave. The trend, being called the ‘GTA flu’ online, comes after players waited 13 years for a new game in the popular franchise.For some players, the GTA 6 launch is worth planning their entire week around. Lander Allgood, a 26-year-old environmental specialist from the Dallas-Fort Worth area, requested two weeks of paid time off in July so he could enjoy the release.Allgood, who has played GTA 5 since he was around 13, compared the new game’s arrival to a major scientific achievement.“We’re basically witnessing, I mean, the Apollo space program of video games,” Allgood told USA TODAY.However, gaming is not his only responsibility. He plans to spend time with his two-year-old son and has arranged for his parents to look after the child from Thursday through Sunday. Once his son goes to bed, Allgood expects to spend hours playing.He is hoping to put in at least 20 hours over the weekend.Connor Folkers, a 22-year-old IT administrator from Iowa, has also arranged his schedule around the launch. He requested leave from November 19 through Thanksgiving and expects to spend more than 24 hours playing.For Folkers, getting enough time with the game before seeing other people’s reactions is important. He wants to experience the story and gameplay without online discussions shaping his opinion.“Really how I treat this game is sort of like a cultural event. You’re going to see this, I presume, everywhere online, whether it be story components or gameplay components, so I want to make sure I have enough time to really experience it for myself without the outside influencing my opinions on it,” Folkers told USA TODAY.He also compared the release to the Super Bowl, explaining how important the event has become for gaming enthusiasts.Not everyone is being upfront about taking a day off. Some players are planning to report sick on November 19 instead of requesting paid leave in advance.GameSquare surveyed 1,000 full-time US employees who identified as gamers. Its findings showed that 10% planned to skip work on launch day, while another 30% were considering taking time off. Among those considering leave, 36% said they would call in sick.BambooHR also found that nearly one in five salaried US workers planned to take time off for the release. Its figures showed that 32% of Gen Z employees and 27% of millennials intended to use paid leave to play.Nicole Csiszar, BambooHR’s director of HR, told USA TODAY that taking planned leave is a normal way for employees to enjoy their time away from work.“That’s a healthy sign,” Csiszar told USA TODAY. “It means people are using PTO the way it’s meant to be used, to step away and do something they enjoy.”She also pointed out why some might choose to call in sick instead.“Requesting PTO in advance means submitting it, waiting on approval and sometimes explaining why you want the day,” Csiszar told USA TODAY. “Calling in sick is one message that morning.”However, not every gamer is willing to put work aside. Ryan Van Dusen, a 42-year-old fifth-grade teacher from Michigan, has no plans to miss classes for the game. He is instead looking forward to playing during the Thanksgiving holiday.“My kids are expected to be in the classroom. I can’t take a day off from my students for this. This is preposterous,” Van Dusen told USA TODAY with a laugh. “In theory, Grand Theft Auto should be a small thing compared to work, family, things that are bigger. I think it’s healthy and good for us to have these small things that we can be excited for too and just to look forward to.”
Article Summary: Nearly one in five salaried workers in the United States plans to take time off for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19. A GameSquare survey also found that 36% of workers considering time off would rather call in sick than request leave. The trend, being called the 'GTA flu' online, comes after players waited 13 years for a new game in the popular franchise.

A fire broke out in an empty postgame tent outside MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday, sending thick clouds of smoke billowing over the venue hours after the New York Jets suffered their fifth consecutive defeat of the NFL season.Videos shared on social media showed large plumes of smoke rising near the stadium in East Rutherford and drifting over the playing field. One video also captured flames and black smoke erupting from the area near the venue.New Jersey State Police said troopers responded to a report of smoke shortly after 5:50 pm near Lot A and the stadium's American Express gate. They found a fire in an empty postgame tent, according to a report by Fox 5 New York.Fire crews brought the second-alarm blaze under control. No injuries or further damage were reported, while the cause of the fire was not immediately known.ESPN reporter Rich Cimini posted on social media that an announcement had been made inside the stadium about a “structure fire” near the adjacent train station. He later advised people to stay away from the stadium's east plaza, on the train station side, as smoke spread across the venue.Around 20 minutes later, he posted that the “situation has been resolved”.An NJ Transit spokesperson, quoted by NY Post said the fire did not disrupt train services in the area.The blaze broke out hours after the Jets lost 31-12 to the Buffalo Bills at MetLife Stadium. The defeat marked their fifth straight loss, leaving them with a 2-8 record for the season.The Jets struggled against the Bills, who secured a 19-point victory. The loss extended New York's losing streak and added to a difficult season for the team.
Article Summary: Fire broke out in an empty postgame tent outside MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday. The blaze sent thick clouds of smoke billowing over the venue hours after the New York Jets suffered their fifth consecutive defeat of the NFL season. No injuries or further damage were reported. The cause of the fire was not immediately known.

Article Title: 'He is my friend': Trump, Putin hold talks ahead of trilateral meeting with Xi on APEC sidelines
Article Text:
Trump Putin hold talks ahead of trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping

Trump-Putin meeting ahead of trilateral talks

Xi and Putin reaffirm strategic partnership

Putin criticises economic restrictions, calls for fairer world order

Nuclear arms control and Iran on trilateral agenda

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump held bilateral talks with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin, ahead of a trilateral discussion with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday.The meeting was held on the sidelines of APEC summit in Chinese city of Shenzhen.Trump expressed optimism ahead of the meeting"A lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start", he said."We will have a second meeting later on," he added.The meeting comes amid heightened diplomatic activity involving Washington, Moscow and Beijing, with the three leaders expected to discuss nuclear disarmament, the Iran conflict, the Russia-Ukraine war and global trade. The proposed trilateral engagement is being closely watched as a possible opportunity to address some of the most pressing geopolitical challenges.Trump arrived at the APEC venue earlier in the day, where he was welcomed by Xi. The US president subsequently met Putin, with the two leaders exchanging handshakes before joining other world leaders for a group photograph.The bilateral engagement between Trump and Putin comes a day after the Russian president held extensive discussions with Xi, reaffirming the strength of Moscow's strategic partnership with Beijing.The Trump-Putin meeting assumes importance as Washington and Moscow seek to address differences over the Ukraine war and the future of nuclear arms control.Trump had indicated before departing for Asia that the proposed discussions with Putin and Xi would cover several major international issues, including nuclear disarmament, Iran, Ukraine and economic relations."We're going to be talking about denuclearisation...We'll talk about Iran," Trump told reporters ahead of his departure.He also identified the Russia-Ukraine war as a key subject of discussion."We'll also talk about my favourite subject, Ukraine. Ukraine is losing. Ukraine and Russia are losing 25,000 souls per month, so we'll be talking about that. We'll also discuss economics and trade," Trump said.The proposed trilateral meeting would bring together the leaders of three major powers at a time when diplomatic efforts to resolve the Ukraine conflict have faced challenges.The prospect of discussions involving Washington and Moscow without Ukraine's direct participation has also raised concerns in Kyiv and among its European partners.Ahead of Trump's arrival, Xi and Putin held bilateral discussions in Shenzhen on Wednesday, reaffirming their commitment to strengthening economic, political and strategic cooperation.Xi described the relationship between China and Russia as resilient amid international uncertainty, saying their ties "stand as firm as a mountain amid wind and rain".He called on both countries to adopt a long-term strategic approach and shoulder greater responsibilities as major powers in shaping the international order."We must firmly shoulder the responsibilities expected of major powers, lead and advance the multipolarisation of the world and the democratisation of international relations," Xi said.Putin, meanwhile, described political cooperation between Moscow and Beijing as constructive despite the challenging international environment."Russian-Chinese political cooperation is working favourably and constructively in a difficult political situation," Putin stated."We are committed to constructive approaches to form a fairer multipolar world order," he added.The two leaders also discussed the need to expand cooperation across sectors, with Xi describing their partnership as a model of equality, mutual respect and mutually beneficial cooperation.According to Russian media reports, the discussions continued over a working breakfast in Shenzhen on Wednesday.Putin also addressed business representatives at the APEC CEO Summit, where he criticised the use of tariffs, sanctions and export restrictions as instruments of geopolitical and economic pressure.He argued that countries were increasingly seeking greater economic sovereignty and independence amid changes in the global geopolitical landscape."The regional model serves as a vivid example of strengthening a fairer, more democratic and equal world order," Putin said, referring to developments in the Asia-Pacific region.The Russian president criticised attempts by established economic powers to restrict the growth of emerging economies, arguing that such measures undermined fair competition and could ultimately hurt the countries imposing them.Putin acknowledged that tariffs, export restrictions and sanctions continued to affect economic development."But they are not capable of fully stopping growth or destroying the economies of the competition," he added.He also expressed expectations of "great use" from the proposed trilateral meeting involving Trump, Xi and himself.The proposed meeting comes at a sensitive moment for international nuclear arms control following the expiration of the New START treaty between the United States and Russia in February 2026.Trump has expressed interest in negotiating a new nuclear arms control framework that would include China alongside Washington and Moscow.However, Beijing has traditionally resisted joining such negotiations, pointing to the considerably larger nuclear arsenals maintained by the United States and Russia.The Iran conflict is another issue expected to feature in the discussions, alongside disagreements over international trade, tariffs, technology restrictions and global supply chains.China has described the proposed trilateral engagement as being of "ground-breaking significance", with the potential to safeguard global peace and promote strategic stability among major powers.The APEC summit has consequently emerged as an important diplomatic platform for Washington, Moscow and Beijing to engage on issues ranging from nuclear security to regional conflicts and the future of the global economic order.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump held bilateral talks with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin, ahead of a trilateral discussion with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The meeting was held on the sidelines of APEC summit in Chinese city of Shenzhen. The proposed trilateral engagement is being closely watched as a possible opportunity to address some of the most pressing geopolitical challenges.

How a slow body clock sends birds the wrong way

Infographic showing clock-shift that occurs during homing flights of shearwaters. The bird begins to home at point A. On the first day of homing, its endogenous clock is calibrated to local time at 30°W. However, the shearwater travels eastwards to 15°W over 6 hours to point B. Here, sunrise happened an hour earlier, so the shearwater’s perceived time lags local time by an hour and the sun is roughly 20° further clockwise than the shearwater expects. Small errors for adults, bigger risks for first-timers

Manx shearwaters flying home from feeding trips can be nudged off course by a kind of jet lag, researchers say. It happens when a bird’s body clock falls out of step with the local time. Tracking data from Manx shearwaters on the west coast of the UK revealed that when the birds returned home to their colonies after trips over the Atlantic, their rapid eastward flights disrupted their sense of time and navigation.When humans get jet lag, we fly across time zones and feel tired and out of sync because our body clock is still running on the old time. Shearwaters seem to have a similar problem. For them, it shows up as a wrong turn over the open sea.A studyfinds that long-distance flights can throw seabirds' internal clocks out of sync, causing navigation errors , it was published in October 2026 on the Oxford University website. It talks about how researchers in Oxford University's Department of Biology analysed 20 years of GPS tracking data from 1,045 breeding shearwaters, covering 3,688 foraging trips. The birds set off from colonies on the west coasts of the UK and Ireland. Some flew about 1,000km west to find food. On the way home, they flew east, back to their nests.Like many animals, shearwaters use the sun as a compass. This is very useful over open water, where there are no roads or landmarks. But the sun moves across the sky during the day, so a bird needs to know the time to work out where the sun should be. The bird’s body clock gives it that information. It is called the circadian rhythm. Birds normally reset their clocks at sunrise. That works well while a bird stays in one place. But when a bird travels quickly east or west, its clock can fall out of sync with local solar time. On the flight home, the shearwaters crossed places where the sun rises earlier. The Oxford release says this can leave their clocks lagging behind local time by up to around one hour.The researchers worked out how a slow clock should change the birds’ sun compass. Then they compared those predictions with the directions the GPS trackers recorded. As the birds travelled east, they tended to drift clockwise from their expected direction. That is what you would expect if their clocks were running behind. The team from the Department of Biology found that when the predicted compass error pointed towards land, the shearwaters flew closer to the coast. When it pointed away from land, they flew further out to sea. So the birds seem to use the sun compass even when familiar land is close by.The errors were real, but they were small. In “Seabirds get jet lag, too — and it can throw them a bit off course,” published by Science News on October 29, 2026, Anirban Mukhopadhyay reports that the birds veered by as much as 15 degrees. The errors were small enough to add only a few kilometres to the journey. They were not enough to stop the shearwaters from finding their way home.Adult birds can fix their mistakes because they keep checking where they are. The Oxford team calculated that a shearwater returning from 1,000 km away with an average compass error of seven degrees would fly only about 5 km further than needed to get within 5 km of its colony.“It’s inherently difficult to study the cognitive processes of animals in the wild, so it’s exciting to realise that if we measure their natural movements carefully enough we can reveal the underlying behavioural mechanisms.” - Co-author Professor Tim Guilford, Department of Biology, Oxford University. The consequences could be more significant for animals that cannot continuously reassess and correct their positions.For example, young birds undertaking their first migration could be particularly vulnerable. Small navigational errors might accumulate over a long journey, potentially shifting their eventual destination by hundreds of kilometres.Researchers do not yet know whether the clock mismatch affects the birds in other ways. Internal clocks control many parts of an animal’s behaviour and body, so the problem could reach beyond navigation. More work is needed to find out. Dr Patrick Lewin, the lead researcher, has said that studying animals that regularly travel long distances could one day help us understand how humans cope with jet lag. “It’s amazing to think that billions of migratory animals look up to the sun for direction, relying on clocks silently ticking away inside them, and that errors in those clocks can cause them to take tiny shifts off course. ” - Lead researcher Dr Patrick Lewin, Department of Biology, Oxford University.
Article Summary: Manx shearwaters flying home from feeding trips can be nudged off course by a kind of jet lag, researchers say. It happens when a bird’s body clock falls out of step with the local time. For them, it shows up as a wrong turn over the open sea.

Article Title: US next aircraft carrier to honour Pearl Harbor hero, Navy rejects name change to Trump

Donald Trump may be getting a battleship named after him, but he will not get his name on America's next aircraft carrier.The US Navy has ruled out renaming its next Ford-class carrier after the president, confirming that the warship will retain the name USS Doris Miller, honouring the Black American sailor who became a hero during Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941.The confirmation comes after months of speculation over a possible name change, with reports in August suggesting that navy officials had discussed renaming the carrier after Trump. The proposal would have replaced the name of Doris Miller, whose bravery during the December 7, 1941, attack on Pearl Harbor made him one of the most celebrated figures in US naval history.The Navy has now put those reports to rest. A spokesperson for acting navy secretary Hung Cao told CNN, "There is no intention to change the name of the USS Doris Miller."The statement effectively rules out the reported proposal and confirms that the next Ford-class aircraft carrier will continue to carry the name of the World War II hero.But why was the carrier's name being reconsidered in the first place? According to CNN's August report, navy officials had held internal discussions about renaming the vessel after Trump. The discussions reportedly came amid a broader push to revisit the navy's ship-naming guidelines, with some officials favouring names of US presidents and senior military leaders for aircraft carriers.The proposal, however, would have meant dropping the name of a sailor whose actions during one of the most defining moments in American military history earned him national recognition.Doris 'Dorie' Miller was serving aboard the USS West Virginia when Japanese forces launched their surprise attack on Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941. Despite having no formal training in operating anti-aircraft guns, Miller took control of one and fired at Japanese aircraft while helping evacuate wounded sailors, including his commanding officer.Miller's bravery earned him the Navy Cross in 1942, making him the first African American sailor to receive the decoration. His recognition was particularly significant at a time when the US navy maintained racial segregation and Black sailors were largely assigned to service roles rather than combat positions.Miller was later killed in November 1943 when a Japanese submarine torpedoed the aircraft carrier USS Liscome Bay during the Battle of Makin.The Navy's decision comes as Trump is already pursuing plans for a new class of warships bearing his name.In December 2025, the president announced the proposed Trump-class battleships as part of his 'Golden Fleet' initiative, with the first vessel expected to be named USS Defiant.The plan would make Trump the namesake of an entirely new class of US navy warships, even as the Navy has ruled out putting his name on the next Ford-class aircraft carrier.
Article Summary: The US Navy has ruled out renaming its next Ford-class carrier after the president. The warship will retain the name USS Doris Miller, honouring the Black American sailor who became a hero during Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor. The confirmation comes after months of speculation over a possible name change.

Article Text:

What was meant to be a routine morning commute turned into a life-changing medical emergency for a New Jersey woman who was left battling for her life after the very people who were supposed to help her, allegedly mistook her stroke symptoms for signs of intoxication. It was followed by a disastrous delay in medical treatment that left her permanently disabled and needing round-the-clock care. Years later, she was awarded millions in damages by a jury. But the state is now pushing back against that decision, arguing the trooper who made the arrest shouldn’t be legally liable for it.According to The Independent, Cheryl Lynn Rhines was driving from her home in Jersey City to her job in Florham Park on October 17, 2017. The 48-year-old is a senior marketing executive for German chemical firm BASF. While driving along the New Jersey Turnpike extension, she suddenly developed signs of a severe stroke.Rhines pulled over near Interstate 78 in Newark as she deteriorated. Her car finally hit a guardrail along the road and kept going.Court documents cited by The Independent say New Jersey State Police troopers arrived about 30 minutes later.They said they found Rhines having trouble communicating and showing clear physical signs such as facial droop, trouble moving and confusion.She said in her lawsuit the stroke impacted the right side of her body, making it difficult for her to follow instructions or control the vehicle. She was also said to be unable to speak properly and only able to give limited answers. Trooper Jennifer Albuja, however, suspected Rhines was under the influence of some unknown substance.According to The Independent, Rhines was taken out of her car, handcuffed and taken into police custody instead of going straight to the hospital.Her attorneys said the trooper did not realize how serious her medical condition was, given numerous visible signs of a stroke. The lawsuit also claimed officers said Rhines was being uncooperative and suggested she was purposely making things difficult.The Independent reported that Rhines allegedly struggled to keep herself under control as she was thrown onto the hood of her car. Her lawyers also said she had bruises on her arms, knee and shin that were noted when she was finally given medical treatment.Instead of being taken to a nearby emergency stroke center, Rhines ended up at the New Jersey State Police barracks in Somerville. Emergency medical personnel were only called when someone at the station saw her condition.The delay cost Rhines about two and a half crucial hours where she might have had urgent stroke treatment, The Independent reported.The results of the delay in medical care were catastrophic, the report says. Medical professionals were eventually able to break up the blood clot in Rhines’ brain, but the damage had already been done.The Independent said the delay caused “substantial brain injury” and “permanent disability.” Rhines was left with constant difficulties of communication and was unable to continue with her professional career, needing ongoing assistance with daily tasks.In her lawsuit, she contended the officers should have realized she needed immediate medical attention and called for emergency services instead of treating her condition as a possible criminal matter.The case also raised wider issues about police training, emergency response procedures and the duty of officers when confronted with people showing signs of serious medical conditions.The lawsuit ultimately resulted in a huge monetary award. NJ reports that an Essex County jury awarded damages of about $19.1 million in January 2025.But the jury also determined that some of Rhines' injuries were caused by the delay in treatment, reducing the award to about $11.46 million. Further adjustments brought the final judgment to approximately $11.25 million.Superior Court Judge Thomas Vena denied the state’s request for a new trial in April 2025, allowing the judgment to stand.The state is now trying to overturn the judgment before a three-judge panel of the Appellate Division in Trenton. New Jersey filed its appeal in October 2025, stating that Albuja had acted in good faith because Rhines’ slurred speech, disorientation and inability to stand reasonably suggested possible intoxication, NJ report said.The state says the trooper should be immune from prosecution for her actions. Or it has asked for a new trial or a reduction in the damages awarded.Another important point is the jury instructions and the calculation of damages. Article Title: A flaw in the granite forced workers to abandon Thomas Jefferson’s original position on Mount Rushmore; they moved him to the other side of Washington
Article Text:
Moun​t Rushmore as it stands today. Jefferson, second from left, sits on Washington’s left after his move. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons

A mountain carved with dynamite

Mount Rushmore as carving began. The planned Entablature, shown on the right, is a conceptual drawing added to the photo. Image Credits: National Park Service

Plan changes as Jefferson moves

The essay contest

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mount Rushmore might look like a plan that went perfectly, but the road to getting there wasn't without hiccups. The National Park Service’s page on the Entablature idea reads that in 1934, the Thomas Jefferson figure was moved from Washington's right (the viewer’s left) to his left due to inconsistencies in the rock. That one flaw in the granite didn’t just move one face; it ended up changing the entire plan for the mountain.The carving ran from 4 October 1927 to 31 October 1941. According to the National Park Service’s Carving History Page , nearly 400 men and women worked on the project. Blasting was a big part of the process. About 90% of the mountain was carved using dynamite. Powdermen would cut and place specific-sized charges to remove specific amounts of rock. The process continued until there were three to six inches of rock remaining. Then drillers and assistant carvers made holes very close to each other in the granite surface. This process is called honeycombing, and it helped weaken the rock so it could be manually removed. Workers were lowered over the 500-foot-tall surface of the mountain in a bosun’s chair. Even though it was risky, no fatal accidents were reported during the 14 years of construction.Sculptor Gutzon Borglum reportedly had big plans for the mountain. He wanted a large inscription there, the Entablature, along with the faces of the four presidents. It was supposed to be a short history of the United States, carved in letters three feet high. The inscription was planned to sit in an area shaped like the Louisiana Purchase territory. The park service suggests that the inscription was meant to present Mount Rushmore as a national memorial to the country's first 150 years, and not just the lives of four great men. Work started, and in 1930, the year 1776 was carved into the east side of the mountain.In 1934, however, Jefferson had to be moved from the right side of Washington to his left because of the inconsistencies in the rock. This brought on further changes along the way. The spot set for the Entablature had to be taken up by Lincoln. Borglum also said that the words would be too hard to read from below. So, the plan changed again. Now the history would go into the Hall of Records, a room behind the sculpture. But Borglum died in 1941, before the plans for the inscription could be finalised.The plan was for Calvin Coolidge to write the history of the United States. But there were disagreements between Coolidge and Borglum on how it should be worded. Coolidge passed away in 1933 before the wording could be finalised. In 1934, Borglum teamed up with the Hearst newspapers to sponsor an essay contest.The winning words were supposed to be carved somewhere on the mountain alongside the four presidents. Once the winners were announced and the prizes awarded, Borglum decided against carving anything into his monument.There was one winner who left a strong impression. A young Nebraskan named William Andrew Burkett won the college-age category. He wrote his essay when he was a student at the Omaha University Law School in 1934. Burkett donated a bronze plaque of his essay on 4 July 1971. The plaque now hangs on the Borglum View Terrace, which was the site of the first studio at Mount Rushmore. The story shows how even a famous landmark was shaped by setbacks that are often lost in the pages of history.
Article Summary: Mount Rushmore was carved from 4 October 1927 to 31 October 1941. Nearly 400 men and women worked on the project. In 1934, the Thomas Jefferson figure was moved from Washington's right (the viewer’s left) to his left due to inconsistencies in the rock. The spot set for the Entablature had to be taken up by Lincoln.

In Envigado, Colombia, Santiago Rojas spent 32 years transforming an old family property into a house covered with stones. Known as Casa Santiago y Gloria or La Casa de las Piedritas, the home became a reflection of a childhood dream and a promise he made to his wife, Gloria Ochoa. Rojas added stones to the property every day gradually, giving the distinctive appearance that attracted visitors from different places. The house was more than 150 years old, according to the account featured by Travel Is Life. Its transformation began after Rojas fulfilled a wish he had carried since childhood: buying the property from his aunt.Rojas was born in San José, Envigado. The house that later turned out to be La Casa de las Piedritas belonged to his aunt. He often assured her as a child that one day, when he grew up and earned money, he would buy that house. He finally made the dream come true and the house became the fulfilment of a promise he had made as a child. Rojas purchased the land and gifted it to Gloria, his wife, before starting the long work on its transformation. The profile by Gente in 2021 explains the background of the project. It says that Rojas promised Gloria a house made of stones and to bring her a flower each day.Moreover, the stones have their own sentimental value. Every time Rojas visited her and found her door shut, he would throw a stone against the window to show that he was here. Some of the stones have allegedly been preserved and have become part of the house.The development of the land was gradual. A 2017 report by Gente described La Casa de las Piedritas as a project that Santiago Rojas had been developing for nearly three decades. He had promised his wife Gloria that he would build her a house made of stones. According to him, he was developing “the most beautiful stone house in the world” for himself and Gloria. Stones turned out to be the main elements of the house. Rojas continued working on his property throughout all those years, turning it into what he was imagining.This work was an example of Rojas’ patience and determination to fulfil the promise. A Gente report published after Rojas’s death in May 2022 also lists the materials used to build the house. In addition to stones, there were cement, adobe, bamboo, cane, tiles, roofing material, construction waste, stained glass and even eyeglass lenses. Rojas was working on all these materials, giving them a special shape.Eventually, the house turned into a known attraction in the neighbourhood of San José, Envigado. Tourists were drawn by the unique stone building and the tale of how it was made. Rojas warmly received visitors and enjoyed the attention given to his home. Rojas claimed in an interview with Gente that he was proud that his house had become a landmark because of his dream that came true. Gente reported on May 10, 2022, that Rojas had died. His work was kept in Envigado as a permanent attribute of the neighbourhood culture. La Casa de las Piedritas was constructed based on Rojas’ childhood dream of having a certain house and the promise to build a special place for Gloria. Having worked for 32 years, Rojas left behind a house filled with the history of their love, stone after stone.
Article Summary: Colombian mason Santiago Rojas spent 32 years transforming an old family property into a house covered with stones. The home became a reflection of a childhood dream and a promise he made to his wife, Gloria Ochoa. Rojas added stones to the property every day gradually, giving the distinctive appearance that attracted visitors.

Article Title: In 2002, Kentucky researchers examined 20 treated subgrade sections across 14 road sites; after 8–15 years, treated soil’s CBR ranged from 24 to 59, versus 2 for untreated soil

Researchers examined 20 treated road sections

Treated soil recorded a much higher

CBR

value

Most road sections remained in good condition

Findings supported the long-term value of soil stabilisation

Roads in Kentucky. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Roads depend on the soil beneath them to support traffic and prevent pavement damage. When the underlying layer is weak, repeated vehicle loads can contribute to cracking, rutting and surface deterioration. In a 2002 study, researchers at the University of Kentucky examined whether chemical treatments could improve road subgrade strength over the long term. They studied 20 treated sections across 14 sites where the pavements had already been in service for approximately 8 to 15 years. The findings appeared in Long-Term Benefits of Stabilizing Soil Subgrades , published in June 2002 by the Kentucky Transportation Center. Tommy C. Hopkins, Tony L. Beckham, Liecheng Sun, Bixian Ni and Barry Butcher conducted the research. The full report is available through the University of Kentucky’s UKnowledge repository Chemical stabilisation of road subgrades had been used in Kentucky since the mid-1980s to improve foundation strength. The study aimed to find out whether these improvements had lasted after years of traffic and weathering. The researchers studied 20 chemically treated sections at 14 road sites. Scientists took approximately 455 samples of soil cores from both treated soil and non-treated soil beneath it.In the experiments, scientists used several types of chemical stabiliser: hydrated lime, Portland cement, a combination of hydrated lime and Portland cement and a by-product of hydrated lime production known in the study as MKD.One of the tests measured the California Bearing Ratio (CBR), which compares the penetration resistance of the soil with that of standard crushed rock. Engineers use it to judge how well soil can support load under a road and a higher value generally means a stronger subgrade. In terms of CBR at the 85th percentile, chemical treatment of the subgrade resulted in in-situ values of CBR that ranged from 24 to 59. The corresponding value of soil beneath the layer of treated soil was only two. Hence, treated soil gave results that were about 12 to 30 times better than those of untreated soil. A falling weight deflectometer was also used to determine how the pavement behaved under load. Back-calculated modulus values for the treated layers were about twice those of the untreated soil.Additionally, pavement condition status was considered along with soil strength test results. Twelve out of 14 roadways had pavements in good condition, according to Kentucky Transportation Cabinet criteria. The research team projected that these pavements would still be rated good at the end of their 20-year design period. Two roadways had a thin overlay of asphalt pavement after about 15 years. There was a difference in the soil layer condition as well. The untreated subgrade had a soft, moisture-affected surface layer, while the treated soils did not. This contributed to the better engineering characteristics of the chemically stabilised materials.The study offered proof in the field that chemical improvement of road foundations would last through many years of use. The research included data from multiple locations with various stabilisers. This enabled the engineering personnel to evaluate the effectiveness of treatment through the test period rather than short laboratory tests. The research team also developed structural layer coefficients for estimating the load-carrying capacity of pavements built over chemically treated foundations.The values were tested using sections of the roads that were designed with thinner pavement.The research indicated that stabilisation of the road helped in maintaining the structural integrity of the road foundation. This does not imply that all treatments would be equally effective. Main factors such as composition of soil, moisture content, methods of construction and traffic loading have an impact on performance. The study helped transportation departments understand that the benefits of soil stabilization would last long after the construction process. It might also provide the designers of pavement structures with more design options.
Article Summary: Researchers at the University of Kentucky examined whether chemical treatments could improve road subgrade strength over the long term. Chemical stabilisation of road subgrades had been used in Kentucky since the mid-1980s to improve foundation strength. The study aimed to find out whether these improvements had lasted after years of traffic and weathering.

Article Title: Florida battles historic flooding as storms move further north
Article Text:
In Central Florida, residents face rising water levels from recent heavy rain, prompting evacuation alerts.

Water levels across central Florida continued to rise on Friday even as rainfall eased, prompting authorities to warn residents in flood-prone areas along the state's longest river to prepare for possible evacuations.The city of Rockledge urged people living in its low-lying western neighbourhoods to be ready to leave their homes while conditions remained safe.Thousands of residents could be affected as days of heavy rainfall flow into the St. Johns River and its surrounding lakes, according to meteorologists from the National Weather Service in Melbourne."We're so concerned with the Saint Johns River," said Will Ulrich, a warning coordination meteorologist in Melbourne. He warned that the large volume of water would cause the river to keep rising over the coming days.Near Cocoa, the river crossed its previous record level set in 1953 on Thursday. The National Weather Service forecast that flooding would continue until early next week.Heavy rainfall has already inundated large parts of Florida's Atlantic coast, leaving some residents stranded in floodwaters in the northeastern region of the state.Flood warnings and watches issued by the National Weather Service cover an area stretching nearly 200 miles (320 kilometres), from south of Melbourne to Jacksonville. Forecasters expected another 6 inches (15 centimetres) of rain in some areas through Saturday, while isolated locations could receive as much as 12 inches (30 centimetres).Hundreds of emergency personnel were deployed along the coast to assist affected communities.In the Florida Shores neighbourhood of Edgewater, police officers waded through knee-deep water on Friday to pull residents to safety using a small boat. Further south in Brevard County, rescue teams used airboats to navigate flooded roads and reach stranded people. Authorities had carried out nearly 100 high-water rescues in the area a day earlier.Some parts of Florida's east coast have received more than 17 inches (43 centimetres) of rain since Tuesday, according to preliminary National Weather Service figures. The state had also experienced heavy rainfall earlier this month, with several locations already recording their wettest November on record.* Flooding disrupts Thanksgiving preparationsThe severe flooding has also disrupted holiday plans for residents preparing for Thanksgiving.Sara Hernandez had decorated her home and purchased groceries for the holiday before floodwaters reached her front and back doors on Thursday morning. By Friday, several inches of water had entered her house.She said she was uncertain about how she and her family would manage the situation."I have never ever seen this much water in the 25 years I've been in Florida," Hernandez said in a message. "It's never flooded here."Hernandez, who runs a cleaning business, said removing the water would be difficult and she could not afford to replace damaged household appliances. She had hoped to make the holiday special for her four children."At least we are safe and dry," she said while staying at her brother-in-law's house.Meanwhile, rain could affect much of the US Eastern Seaboard during the holiday week, as millions of Americans prepare to travel.The low-pressure system responsible for Florida's heavy rainfall was expected to move northeast over the weekend, bringing rain to the coastal areas of Georgia and the Carolinas, said Scott Kleebauer, a meteorologist at the National Weather Service's Weather Prediction Center in Maryland.Another weather system moving in from the Atlantic could bring further rainfall from the mid-Atlantic region to New England on Sunday and Monday.Forecasters said the system could develop into a subtropical or tropical storm, bringing strong winds, dangerous surf and coastal flooding to the southeastern and mid-Atlantic regions through early next week.Meteorologists are also monitoring the possibility of a third coastal system developing around the middle of next week and moving from the Southeast towards New England.Kleebauer said the third system could be stronger and potentially affect several areas on Wednesday and Thanksgiving Day.* Flood risk could continue into 2027The storms affecting Florida this week have been driven by persistent high pressure over Virginia, along with a low-pressure system and a stationary front in the Gulf. Together, these weather conditions have pushed a continuous flow of moisture from the ocean across the Florida Peninsula.The weather pattern is also linked to El Niño, a natural warming of the Pacific Ocean near the equator that influences weather conditions across the world. Florida's dry season generally lasts from October to May.However, the slow-moving St. Johns River poses a prolonged flooding threat to communities along its banks. Forecasters expect El Niño conditions to continue through the spring.Ulrich said the heavy rainfall had left the soil saturated even before the beginning of Florida's usual dry season. He warned that flooding along the river could continue well into the new year and possibly through 2027.Meanwhile, heavy rainfall also caused widespread flooding across parts of California, including areas between Los Angeles and San Francisco. Several neighbourhoods were inundated, forcing motorists to abandon vehicles stranded in floodwaters. A long section of coastal Highway 1 was also closed because of rockfalls and mudslides.Two people, a man and a woman, were found dead in Chino on Friday following the heavy rainfall, according to the San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department.The woman had been swept downstream after rescue teams failed to save her from the water a day earlier. The man's body was discovered during the search for her. Authorities had not immediately released further details about the man.
Article Summary: Heavy rainfall has already inundated large parts of Florida's Atlantic coast, leaving some residents stranded in floodwaters. Authorities warn residents in flood-prone areas along the state's longest river to prepare for possible evacuations. Flooding disrupts holiday plans for residents preparing for Thanksgiving.

Article Title: A 38-year-old New York nurse who had already run more than 60 marathons completed all seven World Marathon Majors in 2026 while pregnant, finishing her hometown race at 34 weeks with her doctor's appr

Pregnant at 34 weeks, New York nurse completes all seven major marathons

How the plan shifted

How she managed the races

In this photo provided by Max Guliani, Deirdre Keane runs during the New York City Marathon in New York. AP/PTI(AP11_19_2026_000262B)

What made the challenge possible

Why the story matters
